Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor / residency options for HIPAA/GLBA/FERPA review

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Greenfield's privacy team asked for a single-page matrix that shows: (1) which Redwood subprocessors touch customer data for each product surface we might use (inference API, embeddings, logging/retention), (2) where that data can be hosted (US-only, EU+US, customer VPC), and (3) whether a HIPAA BAA path / GLBA addendum / FERPA language exists or is planned.

Two asks to make the review fast:
- Can you provide a short matrix and call out items that require Legal pathing (e.g., SOC 2 + BAA for PHI, residency commitments for GLBA)?
- For any items without a direct commitment, please propose a phased remediation timeline (quick fixes vs. product work).

If you can send the matrix and any draft DPA language by COB Monday (US ET) we can circulate to our security and legal.

Best,
Sara Thompson
Senior Vendor Risk Manager
Greenfield Bank

Subject: Re: Subprocessor / residency options for HIPAA/GLBA/FERPA review

Laura — attaching first-pass matrix and a short visual for residency options. See attachments: subprocessor-matrix-v1.xlsx, residency-options-visual.png.

High-level summary from engineering/product perspective:
- Inference API: Core runtime (redwood-runtime-prod) is the only subprocessor that touches raw request tokens for hosted mode. Embeddings pipeline writes token metadata to analytics for billing; that can be disabled per-account.
- Logging/Retention: Retention is configurable; default is 30 days for logs/metrics. We can offer 0-day retention for PII/PHI via dedicated retention config (requires config flag + SIEM integration) — P0 (2–4 weeks) for config change, P1 (2–3 months) for automation.
- Residency: US-only hosting (regional pinned) is available out-of-the-box for hosted customers in our us-east and us-west clusters. EU+US hybrid requires replication and is a P1 product work item (2–3 months) unless the customer opts for Dedicated or Private VPC. Private VPC with customer-managed keys and regional-only routing is immediate via Redwood Private (requires onboarding + contract).

Legal flags:
- HIPAA/BAA: We have a BAA path for Dedicated customers (SOC 2 + BAA + audit log export). For hosted, BAAs require additional controls (data segregation + retention guarantees) — I marked this as P1.
- GLBA: Residency is the primary ask; GLBA also expects annual audits and proof of controls. Recommend proposing a GLBA addendum scoped to region + audit support (Karthik, please advise wording).
- FERPA: For K12 use, we need explicit subprocessor disclosure and clear prohibition of downstream analytics for student data in hosted tier. Private or Dedicated solves many of these risks.

I also drafted a short DPA language to accelerate review (see redwood-dpa-hybrid-draft.pdf). Suggest we push the matrix + the draft DPA + a 1-page summary to Greenfield Monday.

-Vivek
Director, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Subprocessor / residency options for HIPAA/GLBA/FERPA review

Thanks Vivek — good work. Quick legal/product notes from my side: 

- Attach redwood-dpa-hybrid-draft.pdf: it attempts to cover BAAs, a GLBA addendum clause, and FERPA-specific language (data classification + permitted uses). It is intentionally conservative; legal can relax once they tell us specifics on types of data and retention frequency.
- SOC 2 evidence: we should attach the most recent SOC 2 Type II cert and a short ATO-style control map (I will request the cert from Compliance and attach if we send externally).
- Subprocessor wording: for high-risk verticals we should supply a CSV (subprocessor, role, region) and a bullet that the list is refreshed monthly with certified subprocessors. That will help their vendor risk tool ingest automatically.

Open asks before we send to Greenfield: 
1) Karthik — please propose a short GLBA addendum paragraph we can include in the DPA draft (audit support + residency statement).
2) Vivek — confirm that embeddings metadata write can be disabled immediately per-account and note any residual logs that would require dev work.

I can stitch the one-pager and attach SOC2 cert if we get it by mid-day.

-Marissa
Head of Privacy and Regulatory Affairs
Redwood Inference

Quick summary of our recommendations and next steps:
- Short-term (P0, 2–4 weeks): provide CSV of subprocessors and disable embeddings metadata writes on a per-account basis (Vivek will confirm completion). Share SOC 2 Type II attestation in parallel.
- Mid-term (P1, 2–3 months): scoped GLBA addendum and hosted EU+US hybrid hosting option for accounts that require cross-region replication. HIPAA BAA for hosted customers is P1 pending additional segregation controls; BAA for Dedicated is available now.
- Long-term (P2): product-level automation for retention enforcement and audit exports for GLBA customers on hosted tier.

Can we schedule a 30-min call Wednesday (US ET) for Greenfield legal + security to walk the material? If that works I will send a calendar invite with a short agenda.

Best regards,
Laura
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
